note: A dated, unauthenticated observation of the literature lane's three declared search endpoints, taken by hand from a dev host. It is the wire-side backing for scripts/fixtures/search-providers.json: each declared request below was built by the lane's own SEARCH_PROVIDERS[].build (the code the shipped lane runs) and sent to the vendor with a deliberately invalid credential, and every reply is verbatim. It records one moment — not a subscription to the vendors, and not an input to any gate: no test or CI job replays it against a network. scripts/assert-external-health.test.mjs section 16 reads it offline, only to check that the evidence still describes the request the lane builds today.
statement: Unauthenticated observation, not a captured successful response. No credential existed on the host that ran this probe, so nothing below is a successful search: every reply is a rejection. A rejection still discriminates — a refusal that names the credential, or that arrives where a wrong path would have returned 404, proves the endpoint and the credential placement are the ones the vendor routes on. What it cannot prove is listed under doesNotProve, per provider.
client: fleet-store/1.0 (linux; node) — the lane's own User-Agent; the transport adds its own headers (accept-encoding, connection, …), which are not part of the contract
credentialNote: probe-not-a-credential-0000 — a well-formed value that is not a credential, so every status below is the vendor's answer to the request rather than a search result
proves: each declared host and path routes: Tavily answered POST /search with 401 where /searchX returned 404, and Google answered GET /customsearch/v1 with a key error where /customsearch/v1x returned 404

the credential travels in the place the fixture puts it: Brave's declared path names x-subscription-token as a required header when it is missing and rejects the token as invalid when it is present; Tavily reaches its auth layer through Authorization: Bearer; Google validates the key query parameter as an API key

each vendor answered the declared path with the envelope family the lane parses (JSON, with an error object on a refusal) — the lane's non-200 path needs only the status, but a bot check or a redirect is exactly what changes the content type
doesNotProve: acceptance: no successful response was captured, so no 200 envelope, result field, or rate-limit status is confirmed here
the recorded 200 bodies in search-providers.json, which remain transcriptions of the vendors' documentation — a green sensor still means only that the lane matches that transcription
any parameter the vendor checks after the credential (result count, query syntax)

probes.label: control: declared path, credential header removed
control: path that does not exist, declared header kept

proves: the credential header is X-Subscription-Token: with the header removed the declared path returns 422 VALIDATION whose error lists loc ["header","x-subscription-token"] and msg "Field required" — the vendor naming the header it wants

the endpoint is live and authenticates on that header: the declared request with the invalid token returns 422 SUBSCRIPTION_TOKEN_INVALID with meta.component "authentication" — an auth decision, not a routing or a parameter error
doesNotProve: that /res/v1/web/search is the routed path: the identical token on the nonexistent /res/v1/web/searchX returns the identical SUBSCRIPTION_TOKEN_INVALID, so Brave checks auth before routing and this probe cannot tell the two paths apart — an explicit unknown, not a confirmation
anything about the fixture's 429 RATE_LIMITED envelope: a rate limit cannot be reached without a credential
providers.rejectedCase: the fixture's brave.rejected case is the verbatim body of the declared probe (HTTP 422 SUBSCRIPTION_TOKEN_INVALID)

probes.label: control: declared path, credential in the body (the shape this lane used to send)
control: path that does not exist, Bearer kept

proves: the declared path exists and is the vendor's search route: POST /search with the invalid Bearer token returns 401 {"detail":{"error":"Unauthorized: missing or invalid API key."}} where the same request to /searchX returns 404 with no body

the credential is read from Authorization: Bearer — the same invalid token sent as api_key in the JSON body (the shape this lane used to send, and the RESEARCH-2 defect) returns the identical 401, as does an X-Api-Key header, so the header the fixture sends is a credential transport the auth layer reads and the body field is not
doesNotProve: whether the api_key body field is rejected or silently ignored: its 401 is indistinguishable from the no-credential control, so the finding is 'the body shape does not authenticate', not 'the vendor rejects it'
a successful search, the 200 envelope's fields, or Tavily's real rate-limit answer
providers.rejectedCase: the fixture's tavily.rejected case is the verbatim body of the declared probe (HTTP 401 Unauthorized: missing or invalid API key.)

probes.label: control: declared path, no key at all
control: declared path, key in a header instead of the query
control: declared path, num above the documented maximum, invalid key
control: path that does not exist

proves: the declared path exists: GET /customsearch/v1 with an invalid key returns 400 "API key not valid. Please pass a valid API key." (details[].reason API_KEY_INVALID, metadata.service customsearch.googleapis.com) where /customsearch/v1x returns 404 with Google's HTML error page

the credential is read from the key query parameter: the 400 is a key-validation answer, which only happens after a key has been read from where the lane put it; with the parameter absent entirely the answer is different — 403 PERMISSION_DENIED, "Method doesn't allow unregistered callers"
doesNotProve: that num is checked before the key: num=25 (above the documented maximum) returns the same key error, so the lane's MAX_HITS_PER_QUERY cap is an assumption of the fixture, not an observation

whether the key query parameter is the only placement Google accepts: the same invalid key in an X-Goog-Api-Key header also reaches key validation, so the header is read too — the lane's placement is confirmed, its exclusivity is not
providers.rejectedCase: the fixture's google-cse.rejected case is the verbatim body of the declared probe (HTTP 400 API key not valid)
